Alice P.: Quick sync — packaging and upgrade paths for private deployments. Need to pick a default approach for customer-managed networking vs Redwood-managed overlay. TL;DR: customers keep asking for minimum ops and smooth upgrades.
Ravi K.: +1. We should decide tradeoffs for OTA upgrades to on-prem agents. Key constraints: no inbound ports, cert rotation, and offline upgrade bundles.
Monica L.: From infra POV, customer-managed VPC is simplest for us (network ownership stays with them) but breaks our rollout automation. Managed-overlay reduces customer effort but increases our NFR surface (routing, peering).
Diego S.: Solutions engineering has seen 3 customers push for a zero-touch upgrade path. They don't want to download tarballs and run migrations. They will pay for managed if reliability is guaranteed.
Eva (sec): Security concerns: if we run an overlay/managed network we must support HSM/KMS integration per-enterprise, end-to-end audit logs, and strict least-privilege. That extends delivery by ~2 quarters unless we scope an MVP.
Jordan (sales): To be clear — high-touch enterprise deals expect private with managed networking + upgrade SLA. Mid-market prefers customer-managed VPC and scriptable upgrades. We should productize both but prioritize the big deals.
Alice P.: Proposal A (conservative MVP): customer-managed VPC, offline upgrade bundles, operator-run checklist, documented rollback steps.
Alice P.: Proposal B (opinionated offering): Redwood-managed overlay with auto-upgrades, feature flags, and optional onboarding service. Higher revenue but higher security/compliance effort.
Ravi K.: Engineering estimate (ballpark): A => 2 sprints infra + 1 sprint docs + runbook. B => 4-5 sprints infra, security gating, and additional SRE runbook.
Monica L.: For A we can reuse current agent lifecycle code and extend the bundle format: 
```
bundle-v1.tar.gz
├─ agent/
├─ configs/
└─ preflight.sh
```
Preflight will validate networking, ports, and KMS endpoints.
Diego S.: Customer onboarding: script for migration path `agent migrate --from v1 --to v2` and a dry-run mode. That covers most ask.
Eva (sec): For B, we need a compliance checklist: KMS design, central audit, mutual TLS between overlay nodes, and SOC/PenTest plan. Otherwise security won't sign off.
Jordan (sales): Can we sell an "upgrade SLA" add-on for A? Helps close deals and reduces urgency on B.
Alice P.: Decision points we need today: 1) MVP scope (A or B) 2) whether to offer upgrade SLA as add-on 3) gating criteria for moving from A -> B.
Ravi K.: My vote: ship A as MVP, include a paid upgrade-SLA option, and run a pilot with 2 enterprise customers to validate gaps. Then iterate to B if pilot shows >3 critical gaps.
Monica L.: Agree. Action items: I will draft the bundle spec and preflight checks. ETA EOW for an initial doc.
Diego S.: I'll pull together customer ask log (3 high-touch customers) and proposed CLI UX for migration.
Eva (sec): I'll list mandatory security gates and an accelerated path for customers willing to sign a higher-risk acknowledgement.
Jordan (sales): I'll coordinate pilot customers and price the upgrade-SLA.
Alice P.: OK. Finalize: MVP = Proposal A (customer-managed VPC + offline bundles) + optional paid upgrade-SLA. Pilot -> decide on managed-overlay follow-up.
deploy-bot: Deployment notice: created doc `product/private-deploy-mvp-bundle-spec` by Monica L.
Ravi K.: One more thing — need clear rollback semantics in the spec (db schema changes, model cache invalidation). Add a "safe mode" flag in bundles.
Monica L.: noted. Will include `--safe-mode` and a fenced rollback checklist.
Diego S.: +1 on safe mode. Also add a short troubleshooting FAQ for common networking errors.
Alice P.: Thanks team. I'll convert these notes into a short PRD and share for final sign-off tomorrow. :thumbsup:
